question_text: A school library wants a Python program that calculates the fine for a returned book. Books are borrowed for 14 days. The fine is 0.20 CHF for each day late, up to a maximum of 5.00 CHF per book. Staff type in the book's barcode, the date it was borrowed and the date it was returned. The program must run on the library's existing desktop computer and must be ready before the next term starts. Construct a problem specification for this program. Your specification should include a problem statement, constraints and limitations, objectives, input specifications, output specifications and evaluation criteria.
adaptation_rationale: Original question written by Claude (single-agent Chunk 3 continuation, 2026-11-04) for a syllabus statement with no linked question at handover; no historical source question or official marking status claimed.
solution: Problem statement: library staff need to calculate fines for late books quickly and consistently. Constraints/limitations: written in Python; runs on the existing desktop; ready before next term; maximum fine 5.00 CHF per book; 14-day loan period. Objectives: calculate the correct fine for any return; reduce staff calculation errors and time. Inputs: barcode (string, e.g. 8 digits), borrowed date and returned date (valid dates, returned not earlier than borrowed). Outputs: number of days late (0 if on time) and fine in CHF to two decimal places; an error message for invalid input. Evaluation criteria: correct fines for test cases such as returned on day 14 (0.00), day 15 (0.20) and day 50 (capped at 5.00); invalid dates rejected; result shown within one second.

marking_points.criterion: Problem statement identifying the library staff need in context.
At least two constraints/limitations from the scenario (e.g. Python, existing computer, deadline, fine cap/loan period as rules).
An objective/goal of the program (e.g. accurate, consistent fines; saving staff time).
Input specification naming barcode, borrowed date and returned date with type/format or validity rule.
Output specification: days late and fine (formatted CHF) and/or error message.
Measurable evaluation criteria (e.g. boundary test cases 14/15 days, cap at 5.00, invalid input rejected).

acceptable_alternatives: Accept any reasonable format (headings, table or bullet list). Accept justified assumptions (e.g. barcode length) when stated. Each element must be specific to the library scenario to gain the mark.
partial_credit_notes: Award each independent point once, up to 6 marks. Accept equivalent correct wording or valid alternative code. Do not double-credit one idea.

verification.technical: Manual author check of every criterion against the exact statement and all guidance paragraphs; no executable component.
verification.scope: No code is required. Algorithm design and testing are assessed in other B1/B2 statements.
